checks.command: live daemon with the rebuilt binary: run --detached --session work with two '::: ' commands, then list/status/stop

surface: Every session start advances its creation phases in one reactor iteration by default; a phase that ends without a pending worker request no longer waits for the daemon's idle poll.
The loop stops on a pending worker request, an unchanged phase, or a creation that was finished or rejected, so no phase can spin and no polling behaviour changes.
Timing is unchanged for a busy daemon: the shared long-running instance already woke often enough to hide the idle poll.
limitations: The PTY timing harness is an ad-hoc script run outside the repository, not committed tooling; the numbers are wall-clock values from one machine.

The measurements cover session creation on an otherwise idle isolated instance. Machine load and the number of resident sessions were not varied, so the before/after figures are a direct comparison, not a benchmark curve.
New behaviour has no automated coverage; the repository's remaining checks are the Nix build, packaged CLI smoke and Unicode-width checks.
